headline: Negative: outcome-weighted case retrieval does not turn into the lever as memory grows. From 5 to ~130 same-repo sessions, and at 540 sessions with other repositories included, every kNN successor target nets -0.03 to +0.10 calls/session after harm (0-0.3% of calls). The trivial 'most-often-useful command' prior is 3x better (+0.36 [+0.21, +0.51]), and even this lever's hindsight ceiling is only 6% of calls and 4% of $.
metric_name: net tool calls saved per held-out control session, harm-adjusted (failed commands removed in the skip window, minus carrying cost, minus 1 call per wrong/harmful directive), thresholds chosen leave-one-repo-out; 90% bootstrap over sessions

held_out.best_knn_policy: kNN skip-ahead + avoid-what-failed, same-repo memory of all other tasks (~99 sessions), leave-task-out

leave_one_repo_out.thresholds: every number above uses thresholds chosen on the other repositories (leave-one-repo-out)
leave_one_repo_out.note: Memory from other repositories alone is harmful for the skip and summary targets and the prior, and near zero for avoid. Added to same-repo memory it helps the summary on the v2 Haiku subset (+0.31 [+0.06, +0.53] vs -0.07), but the effect is not significant over all 208 sessions (+0.09 [-0.07, +0.24]).

vs_baseline.baseline: U11 + learned reflexes: +1.00 [+0.56, +1.46] Ŝ calls/session post-hoc, +2.11 pre-emptive (Rust replay, 82 v2 Haiku control sessions)
vs_baseline.this_on_comparable_subset: v2 Haiku control sessions (98): best kNN +0.17 [-0.02, +0.37] (skip+avoid, all memory incl. other repos), summary +0.31 [+0.06, +0.53]; the lab prior reaches +0.73 [+0.50, +0.97] with same-repo memory
vs_baseline.crossing: No kNN curve reaches +1.0. Fitted on log2(memory), avoid gains 0.017 calls per doubling and skip-ahead and summary are flat or falling, so the crossing is >10^6 sessions, which means never. Not even the no-harm upper numbers (≤ +0.64) reach +1.0.
vs_baseline.additive_to_u11: Unmeasured. The directives it finds (pytest / npm test / go test / pip install -e .) overlap U11 and the lab prior, so the additive value is at most the numbers above.

hard_coded_parts: Action identity: evals/lab/normalize.py directive_key (hand-written shlex rules, slot regexes, EXPLORE_BASH / DESTRUCTIVE lists). On top of it, a learned equivalence merges keys at potion cosine ≥ 0.95 within one tool.
Candidate safety filter: normalize.directive_eligible, which excludes exploratory and destructive shell. Avoid candidates are restricted to eligible shell commands (tool == Bash).

Measurement only: the lab's usefulness definition (failed call or ≥ 2 exploratory steps in the window), its discovery regex, and 'edit tool'. These are used for scoring and for the lab-prior baseline, never inside the kNN learner.
Drain-style masking of digits and hex runs in tool output before embedding (a generic tokeniser, not a list of errors).
Harm model: 1 call per followed wrong or harmful directive, with uptake assumed to be 1.

loose_every_exploratory_or_failed_step.note: Not reachable: this counts reads of code the agent needed anyway

ceiling.comment: Measured by failed commands, the lever's hindsight ceiling is 6% of calls and 4% of $, below the 15-20% north-star bar even at 100% capture.

pass_rate_effect: Not estimable offline. The directives are command-discovery hints, and nothing here suggests any pass-rate effect.
build_recommendation: Do not build a kNN / case-retrieval engine in Rust, at this or larger memory. Keep the lab's per-repository 'most-often-useful command' reflex (a counting pass, which grows from +0.07 to +0.29-0.36 calls/session with memory here, and re-estimate its rate as sessions accumulate). If anything from this is kept, it is the commands-only whole-session summary as a cheap SessionStart advise (+0.15 [+0.05, +0.26], precision 0.73): expected value about 0.5% of calls, so it is low priority. Spend sprint effort on levers with a larger ceiling than failed-command removal (≤ 6% of calls).
so_what: Shipped, case-based retrieval would save about 0.0-0.1 calls per session (≤ 0.3% of calls and $, 90% CI including 0 at full memory), with no pass-rate effect we can see. We are highly confident it would not survive a live A/B as a meaningful win, and its ceiling (6% of calls) rules it out as the 15-20% lever.
